meta.titre: The Human Skeleton and Joints: Support, Movement and Levers
meta.sous_theme: Skeleton, joint types and the muscles that move them

sections.contenu_markdown: A bike-taxi rider in Douala lifts his arm to wave and bends his knee to put his foot down. Both movements need bones, joints and muscles working together. If a joint were dry and rough, each movement would hurt. Questions about the skeleton and joints appear in the GCE every year, often as short descriptions that you must match to a name. This course gives you the names, the functions and the way the parts work together.

items: Bones are hard and cartilage is firm but flexible.
Muscles contract to become shorter and thicker.
Friction is the force that resists the sliding of two surfaces.

sections.titre: Bones, joints and the muscles that move them
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Functions of the skeleton
The skeleton **supports** the body, **protects** soft organs (the skull protects the brain, the ribs protect the heart and lungs), allows **movement** by giving muscles something to pull on, makes blood cells in the bone marrow and stores minerals such as calcium. The vertebral column has 33 vertebrae: 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 fused in the sacrum and 4 fused in the coccyx.

### Types of joint
| Joint | Movement | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed (immovable) | None | Bones of the skull |
| Slightly movable | Small movement | Between vertebrae |
| Ball and socket | All directions, including rotation | Shoulder, hip |
| Hinge | Back and forth in one plane | Elbow, knee |
| Pivot | Turning from side to side | Between the first two vertebrae of the neck |

### The synovial joint
Freely movable joints, such as the elbow, are synovial joints:
- **Cartilage** covers the bone ends. It is smooth and reduces friction.
- **Synovial fluid**, made by the synovial membrane, lubricates the joint and reduces friction.
- A **capsule** surrounds the joint, and **ligaments** join bone to bone and hold the joint together.
- **Tendons** join muscle to bone.

### Muscles work in pairs
Muscles can only pull. Muscles that pull in opposite directions are called **antagonistic**. At the elbow the biceps and triceps act as a pair.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks which muscle bends or extends the arm
variantes.contenu_markdown: To bend (flex) the forearm the biceps contracts and the triceps relaxes. To straighten (extend) the forearm the triceps contracts and the biceps relaxes. The extensor of the forearm is therefore the triceps.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a description names a movement and asks for a joint
variantes.contenu_markdown: Match the movement: movement in all directions is a ball and socket joint, movement in one plane is a hinge joint, and a turning movement about an axis is a pivot joint. Read the options carefully. A limb that can swing and rotate in many directions is served by a ball and socket joint, while a pivot joint turns about a single axis only.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks what reduces friction at a joint
variantes.contenu_markdown: Two parts do it: the smooth cartilage on the bone ends and the synovial fluid that lubricates them. If the options include only one of them, choose that one, but never choose ligaments or tendons.

sections.enonce_markdown: A girl lifts a full bucket of water from a well by bending her arm at the elbow. Explain how the bones, joint and muscles produce the movement.

etapes.action: Name the joint and its type.
etapes.justification: The question is about the elbow, which moves back and forth in one plane.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The elbow is a hinge joint.

etapes.justification: Muscles work in pairs and only pull.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The biceps and the triceps are the antagonistic pair.

etapes.justification: Bending the arm needs the biceps to shorten.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The biceps contracts and the triceps relaxes.

etapes.action: Say how the force reaches the bone.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The contracting biceps pulls on the forearm bones through its tendon, and the forearm acts as a lever turning about the elbow.

etapes.action: State how the arm is straightened again.
etapes.justification: A muscle cannot push, so a second muscle is needed.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The triceps contracts and the biceps relaxes.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Model answer.** The elbow is a hinge joint. To bend the arm the biceps contracts while the triceps relaxes. The biceps pulls on the forearm bones through its tendon, and the forearm turns about the elbow as a lever. To straighten the arm the triceps contracts and the biceps relaxes, because a muscle can only pull. The two muscles work as an antagonistic pair.

items.pourquoi_faux: Ligaments join bone to bone. It is the tendons that join muscle to bone.
items.correction_markdown: Ligaments join bone to bone, and tendons join muscle to bone.

items.erreur_markdown: Muscles push the bones into position when they contract.
items.pourquoi_faux: A contracting muscle shortens and pulls. It cannot push.
items.correction_markdown: Muscles pull on bones. A second muscle pulls the other way, so muscles work in antagonistic pairs.

items.erreur_markdown: The elbow is a ball and socket joint.
items.pourquoi_faux: The elbow only bends and straightens in one plane, as a hinge does.
items.correction_markdown: The elbow and the knee are hinge joints. The shoulder and the hip are ball and socket joints.

items.erreur_markdown: Synovial fluid holds the bones of a joint together.
items.pourquoi_faux: The fluid is a lubricant. Ligaments do the holding together.
items.correction_markdown: Synovial fluid reduces friction, and ligaments join the bones.

items.enonce_markdown: Match each joint to its type: shoulder, knee, bones of the skull, between two vertebrae.
items.solution_markdown: Shoulder: **ball and socket**. Knee: **hinge**. Skull bones: **fixed (immovable)**. Between two vertebrae: **slightly movable**.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Distinguish between a ligament and a tendon. (b) Explain why the muscles that move the arm are arranged in pairs.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **A ligament joins bone to bone** and holds a joint together, while **a tendon joins muscle to bone** and transmits the pull of the muscle. (b) A muscle can only pull when it contracts and cannot push. One muscle bends the limb and a second muscle, acting in the opposite direction, is needed to straighten it again.

items.enonce_markdown: After an accident, the knee of a patient produces very little synovial fluid and the cartilage on the bone ends has worn thin. (a) State two problems the patient is likely to have. (b) Explain each in terms of the structure of the joint.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Pain and stiffness**, and **restricted or difficult movement**; the joint may also become damaged further. (b) Without the fluid there is no lubricant, so the bone ends rub against each other and friction is high. Thin cartilage can no longer give a smooth surface or cushion the bones, so movement hurts and the bone ends wear away.

items_markdown: The skeleton supports, protects, allows movement, makes blood cells and stores minerals.
Fixed, slightly movable, ball and socket, hinge and pivot are the types of joint to know, with an example of each.
Cartilage and synovial fluid reduce friction at a synovial joint. Ligaments join bone to bone and tendons join muscle to bone.
Muscles only pull, so they work in antagonistic pairs: at the elbow, biceps bends the arm and triceps straightens it.
The vertebral column has 33 vertebrae in five regions.
